evidence.note: Claim: each single-use third-party package (rapidfuzz, radon, model2vec) is imported by exactly ONE ddflow module (the extras-one-adapter contract), held by the archdeps census. Probe: ddflow.services.archdeps.scan on the worktree. Output: rapidfuzz home=adapters.fuzzy importers=(adapters.fuzzy,) violations=(); radon home=adapters.complexity importers=(adapters.complexity,) violations=(); model2vec home=adapters.embed importers=(adapters.embed,) violations=(). CONFIRMED: one importer each == that packages home, violations empty (radon shrinks from one baseline entry to none).

r-adapters (one implementation per function behind a port, home in ddflow/adapters), r-reuse-core (single Registry/fake), r-small-files (each new module under 20 KB) applied. D-adapters-answers (home ddflow/adapters), D-unify strangler ratchets (baselines only shrink). core stays pure (no third-party import).

Fuzzy/Complexity/Embedder ports + default adapters + fakes in ddflow/adapters (+fakes/), re-export files leave core/fuzzy.py, services/complexity_budget.py, services/embed.py as shims/delegators; archdeps THIRD_PARTY_HOMES repointed.
ruff check over all changed ddflow/ + tests/ files: All checks passed. ruff format --check: all formatted.

chunk_findings.detail: The radon row was the recorded single home (`ddflow.services.complexity_budget`) and this change replaces it with `()`. The new radon home is `ddflow.adapters.complexity` (`RadonComplexity`), not “no module”. With input package `radon` imported from `ddflow.adapters.complexity`, this table now expects an empty importer set, so the arch check either fails on that import or no longer pins radon to one module. A second radon import (core or services) is then indistinguishable from the legitimate adapter import, which breaks the one-home ratchet the edit was meant to move, not delete.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_deps.py:323

data.probe: BASELINE pins VIOLATIONS (importers OUTSIDE a declared home), not the home. Home is THIRD_PARTY_HOMES in archdeps.py. radon had no declared home before, so complexity_budget was a violation -> BASELINE had it; this change ADDS THIRD_PARTY_HOMES["radon"]=("ddflow.adapters.complexity",) and the importer becomes that home, so violations shrink to () -- one entry to none. A second radon import re-grows violations and fails the ratchet, so the one-home contract is STRENGTHENED, not deleted. Probe: census scan shows radon home=adapters.complexity violations=().
